To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalytic component of cyclin D/CDK activity is dispensable for chromosomal instability and tumorigenesis.
cyclin D1 can induce chromosomal instability and breast cancer in mice without its catalytic function.
cyclin D1 induces aneuploidity and mammary tumourigenesis through a kinase-independent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oncogenic mechanisms of the cyclin D family of proteins.
the role of cyclin dependent kinases (CDKs) in breast cancer and the development of new therapeutics.
a better understanding of the molecular basis for the oncogenic function of cyclinD1 in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transforming capacity of cyclin D is not solely due to its kinase function.
the transforming capacity of cyclin D is independent of its CDK activity.
the catalytic activity of cyclin D/CDK4/6 is dispensable for CIN and mammary tumourigenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclin D1 has a non-catalytic role in the induction of chromosomal instability and that cyclin D-kinase activity is not necessary for cyclin D1 to transform the mammary gland.
cyclin D1 can induce CIN and mammary tumours in the absence of CDK activity and that this may be mediated by the direct binding of cyclin D to CIN genes.
the catalytic function of cyclin-CDK complexes is dispensable for the induction of CIN and tumorigenesis, and that the non-catalytic functions of cyclin D are important for CIN and tumourigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeting cyclin D1 for the treatment of cancer should not focus on the catalytic activity of cyclin D/CDK complexes but rather on the ability of cyclin D proteins to regulate gene transcription.
the oncogenic potential is not limited to the catalytic function and that cyclin D1 can induce CIN and tumorigenesis in a kinase-independent manner.
the catalytic activity of cyclin D/CDK4/6 is not essential for oncogenic transformation.
